clue.text: Professor trying to land contract

definitions.meaning: one who professes or openly states something, a person making a declaration
in bridge, the player who won the auction plays the hand trying to make the bid contract

explanation.surface: An academic hoping to secure a new employment deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professor' looks like a university title, but here it is one who professes, i.e. states; 'contract' is the bridge term.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb declare: to state openly, and in bridge the side's player who names trumps and plays the contract.

clue.text: One should admit when one is depressed

definitions.text: One should admit when one is depressed

parts.words: One should admit when one is depressed
parts.note: reads as advice about owning up to low spirits, but describes a device that, when pressed down, leads to a visitor being let in

explanation.surface: Advice that a sufferer should confess to feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: The button by a front door that a caller pushes so the householder will let them in.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink available in bars

definitions.meaning: the confection sold in slabs or bars

explanation.surface: A soft drink served in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs; it means slabs of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa made into a hot drink, and the sweet sold in slabs.

clue.text: Extensive range, as well as extreme limits

annotationWithheld.why: Extensive range, as well as extreme limits (5): AND (as well as) is clear, but no clue word gives ES; 'extreme limits' of no printed word yields those letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Extensive range, as well as extreme limits

clue.text: Times, following editor's lead, simple to interpret

indicators.note: the multiplication sign comes after the editor's opening letter
the lead of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times
plain means simple

explanation.surface: Something about the Times newspaper following its editor's lead, easy to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: To make clear or spell out the meaning of something.

clue.text: Is circle apart from line on weather chart?

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a ring without a line counts as a weather symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists draw lines joining points of equal air pressure on weather maps, and those lines have this name.

clue.text: Enjoys oneself on IOM — in Peel, say

parts.note: to sport is to play or amuse oneself
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker having fun on the Isle of Man, in the town of Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man, but here it is John Peel, the huntsman of the song 'D'ye ken John Peel'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Peel was a celebrated Cumbrian huntsman, an outdoor athlete of the field.

clue.text: Result of ignorance among composers

definitions.meaning: the proverb 'ignorance is ...' says not knowing brings happiness
Sir Arthur ... was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.surface: Being among composers makes one ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect happiness, which the proverb says not knowing brings; also the surname of the composer Sir Arthur.

clue.text: He serves a gross King

parts.note: rank means gross or flagrant, as in 'rank stupidity'
ER is the abbreviation for king, Latin rex

explanation.surface: A man waits on a disgusting monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like 144 or disgusting; it is RANK, as in flagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier serving in the ranks rather than an officer.

clue.text: Miscellaneous collection of OT characters

parts.note: Job is an Old Testament figure with his own book
Lot, Abraham's nephew whose wife turned to salt, is in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A random assortment of people from the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests letters; they are two people from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed bundle of items sold together at auction.

clue.text: Ring with no diamonds, say, like some Fabergé pieces

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
in bridge a hand with no cards in a suit, diamonds for example, is called a void

explanation.surface: A ring without its gemstones, compared to jewelled Russian ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring with no diamonds' suggests a stripped jewel, but 'no diamonds' is the bridge term for an empty suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabergé is famous for its jewelled Imperial eggs, and egg-shaped is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Advertising in advance

definitions.meaning: publicising a product, a marketing campaign
a step up in rank at work

explanation.surface: A note about marketing done ahead of a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both publicity work for a product and being raised to a higher job or rank.

clue.text: Reserves high place for publications

parts.note: to book a seat is to reserve it
tall means high

explanation.surface: Someone books a lofty spot where printed matter is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk or stand selling newspapers and magazines, as at a railway station.

clue.text: Head of state moves to centre, in a sense

indicators.note: the opening letter of state, its head, travels to the middle of the word

parts.note: taken as written, the word whose opening letter shifts

explanation.surface: A political leader relocates to the middle ground, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' reads as a president; it means the S of STATE, which 'moves to centre' to give TA-S-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses alongside sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: The intrigue thickens!

parts.note: plays on 'the plot thickens': the word means both a secret love affair and, in cookery, a binding agent such as egg yolk that thickens a sauce

explanation.surface: A dramatic cry that the story is getting more complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an illicit affair, an intrigue, and also the culinary thickener made from yolks or cream.

clue.text: System of employment in the women's dress business?

definitions.meaning: working in rotas covering day and night
a shift is a simple straight dress, so making them would be work in that line

explanation.surface: Asks what job arrangement the women's clothing trade uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rota-based labour in rotating periods, and humorously labour on making loose straight frocks.

clue.text: Instrument piper's child reproduced

indicators.note: made again, so the name appears twice in a row

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Tom, Tom, the piper's son, stole a pig

explanation.surface: A musician's son copies a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduced' hints at a child having children; it means the name is said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall drum beaten with the hands, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: As a rule, not many take part in it

definitions.text: As a rule, not many take part in it

parts.words: As a rule, not many take part in it
parts.note: 'as a rule' seems to mean usually, but means government; a form of rule in which only a few share power

explanation.surface: A remark that usually few people join in some activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by a small elite group.

clue.text: Confounded nuisance, initially, in savage bears

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for savage carries the letter within it

parts.note: feral means wild or savage

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word nuisance

explanation.surface: A damned nuisance from the start among wild bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like animals; it is the container verb, putting N inside FERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild old-fashioned expletives meaning damned, as in 'that infernal noise'.

clue.text: For every one, can it pass away?

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
I is the Roman numeral for one
'can it!' is slang for be quiet, the same as sh

explanation.surface: A question asking whether something can disappear for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can it' looks like part of the question; it is slang for 'shut up', i.e. SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To die, a gentle synonym for expiring.

clue.text: After trout, serving Americans regional dish

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the old woman

parts.note: an old trout is an unpleasant old woman, a hag
GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: A fish course followed by food served to American visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trout' looks like the fish; it is slang for an old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish dish of offal, oatmeal and spices cooked in a casing.

clue.text: Dombeys, for example, seen round one residence

indicators.note: the man-and-son letters are placed around the numeral

parts.note: in Dickens's novel 'Dombey and Son' the Dombeys are a man and his son, run together
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Characters from Dickens are spotted near a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: Dombey and Son is a Charles Dickens novel; the surface makes 'Dombeys' sound like a family seen near a house, but they stand for its title pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand house, a large and imposing dwelling.

clue.text: Conductors? For new trams, that is

indicators.note: new arrangement of the letters of trams with the Latin abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Asks whether bus or tram conductors are on the new trams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductors' suggests ticket collectors on trams; it means orchestral ones. 'new' rearranges TRAMS with IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian plural for masters of music, the leaders of orchestras.

clue.text: Controlled by banks, this divides our capital

definitions.text: Controlled by banks, this divides our capital

parts.words: Controlled by banks, this divides our capital
parts.note: seems to be about money and finance, but describes the river flowing between riverbanks through London

explanation.surface: Seems to be a complaint that the banks split the nation's wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: London's river runs between its banks and splits the city into north and south.

clue.text: Dismissal for Indian test opener

parts.note: the Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word test

explanation.surface: An umpire's decision dismissing an Indian batsman at the start of a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of an Indian Test opener misleads: 'Indian' is a Native American people and 'test opener' is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt slang order to go away, telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Critic of previous generation

definitions.meaning: Walter ... was a Victorian essayist and art critic
Latin for father, a parent of the generation before

explanation.surface: A critic from an older generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Pater was a Victorian aesthete and reviewer, and the word is old public-school slang for one's father.

clue.text: Fruitful result of putting situation to judge in hearing

parts.note: in golf, putting is done on the green

indicators.note: signals the word for judge is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to gauge is to estimate or judge

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the outcome of laying a case before a judge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting situation to judge in hearing' reads as legal procedure; 'putting' is golf, and 'in hearing' signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of plum, and so a product of a fruit tree.

clue.text: Chemist with no beryllium left

parts.note: taken as written
Be is the chemical symbol for beryllium

explanation.surface: A scientist runs out of beryllium.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and founded the prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was a Swedish scientist and inventor of dynamite.

clue.text: One way follows another for churchman

indicators.note: the numeral and street come after the word for a way

parts.note: another way, a method, being a manner of doing something
I is the Roman numeral for one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Seems to say one road comes after another, leading to a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley.

clue.text: Philosopher saved in dangerous situation

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., the English Renaissance philosopher and essayist
the idiom 'save one's ...' means to escape from danger, so this is what gets saved

explanation.surface: A thinker is rescued from peril.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was the Elizabethan thinker, and the cured pork is what the idiom says is rescued in a tight spot.

clue.text: One 6 played by another

definitions.meaning: 6 down is a sportsman; the oarsman who sets the rowing rate is one such sportsman
a shot in golf, tennis or cricket is played by a sportsman

explanation.surface: One athlete is outplayed by a second.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' refers to the answer of 6 down, a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The rower nearest the stern who sets the pace has this title, and the word also means a single hit of a ball.

clue.text: I'd set about ally so false

indicators.note: the letters are set about, i.e. arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to turning on a partner, and being untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' rearranges I'D and ALLY SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being untrue to one's friends or country, unfaithful.
